audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Binary username-set probe does not identify hidden user-ID association; Covariance probability proof and zero-mean gradient premise do not establish mechanism.
limitations: P1 — Binary username-set probe does not identify hidden user-ID association — Counterevidence: Higher post-tuning accuracy supports representation change
P1 — Binary username-set probe does not identify hidden user-ID association — Counterevidence: Actual association memory not ruled out

P1 — Binary username-set probe does not identify hidden user-ID association — Counterevidence and alternatives: The 85.5/82.0 pre-tuning and higher post-tuning probe results support representation/separability changes, not identification of which paired ID was retained. Zero direct ID-answer accuracy neither proves absence of latent associations nor supplies independent positive association evidence.
P2 — Covariance probability proof and zero-mean gradient premise do not establish mechanism — Counterevidence: Gaussian small-sample covariance phenomenon can be locally proved
P2 — Covariance probability proof and zero-mean gradient premise do not establish mechanism — Counterevidence: Observed gradient and representation changes remain descriptive evidence

P2 — Covariance probability proof and zero-mean gradient premise do not establish mechanism — Counterevidence and alternatives: The qualitative Gaussian covariance-fluctuation phenomenon is true under nondegeneracy and locally repaired here. An extra optimum/orthogonality premise might force a zero residual mean in a special model, but no such premise is supplied for Eq.(3). Neither covariance nor a gradient change identifies persistent content retention.
